summary: Learn to compare benefit options, estimate costs, and frame measurable outcomes. Explore the five-day social assistance program design course.
lede: Social assistance program design turns poverty and vulnerability evidence into costed benefit options with measurable outcomes. For policy officers, program designers, and public finance analysts, it provides a way to compare eligibility and transfer choices, estimate fiscal costs, and connect program goals to household outcomes. You will use benefit-incidence analysis, build cost scenarios in Excel, map delivery and grievance risks, and prepare a decision brief with a results framework.
audienceIntro: This course suits professionals who shape social assistance policy, assess benefit options, or translate program objectives into budgets and operating plans. It is designed for intermediate-level practitioners with some exposure to social protection, public finance, or program delivery.
modules: ILO Recommendation No. 202 and Design Purpose
OECD DAC Criteria for Design Review
prerequisites: Prior exposure to social protection, public finance, program planning, or monitoring and evaluation is recommended. No coding or programming is required. Familiarity with spreadsheet formulas is useful for the Excel costing exercise.
